summary: R4-F1 and R4-F2 are resolved: the faulty owning-element scanner is gone, and the comparison fixture now places the expression before `autoFocus`; the focused suite passes 19/19. The revert intentionally broke cross-element discrimination, so same-file/same-rule replacements now pass. That limit is accurately represented in the code, fixture, README, and canonical gate documentation, and the build/.wxt attribution honestly scopes reproducibility to the tree plus cache-regeneration procedure. However, the final verification summary still materially understates the reverted a11y gap.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md § Triage governs: render EVERY finding as a full table row, never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone; max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: The final evidence still narrows the reverted gap to same-element replacements
findings.body: This summary says only replacements on the same element are missed. After the revert, `scripts/a11y-gate.mjs:122-131` contains no owning-element discriminator, and `scripts/a11y-gate.test.mjs:171-179` explicitly requires an `input` → `textarea` replacement in the same file to PASS. The committed evidence therefore contradicts its later R4 appendix and the canonical documentation, allowing readers to over-credit the hard gate's replacement coverage.
